summary: Singles' Day sales grow just 4.8% as shoppers buy AI gadgets, chipmaker SMIC posts record revenue, and Shenzhen prepares to host Trump, Xi and Putin.
body: China's Singles' Day shopping festival, the world's biggest, grew slowly this year. Data firm Syntun estimates sales of 1.78 trillion yuan (about US$267 billion) between Oct 7 and Nov 11, up 4.8%, compared with 14.2% growth last year; the big platforms no longer publish their own totals.[^1] AP notes that retail sales grew only 1.1% in the first nine months of the year, home prices are about 20% below their 2021 peak, and youth unemployment is around 18%.[^2]

What people bought is telling. JD.com sold more than 50 million AI-related products, sales of AI PCs, cameras and glasses more than doubled, and sales of "token packages" (prepaid use of AI models) rose more than tenfold.[^1] My read: AI is becoming an everyday purchase in China even while families stay careful with big spending.

On the supply side, SMIC, China's largest chipmaker, reported record quarterly revenue of about $3.2 billion, up 34%, with its factories running at about 97% of capacity, and expects 2026 revenue above $12 billion; its co-CEO credits AI demand and China's push to make its own chips.[^3] That push may matter more after Nvidia's CEO resigned this week amid a spy scandal: IDC data cited by Rest of World show Huawei already had 28% of China's AI-chip shipments in the first half of 2026, against Nvidia's 34%.[^4]
Shenzhen, China's tech hub, will also host Presidents Trump, Xi and Putin for their first three-way meeting next week at the APEC summit; US officials say they do not expect an agreement.[^5]

reads.title: China's Singles' Day shopping festival struggles to shake off weak consumer spending
reads.summary: Why Chinese shoppers are holding back, with the numbers on retail sales, home prices and youth jobs behind the slow festival.
